messages:
Alex Kim: FYI RFC follow-up — proposing we extract the dashboard renderer out of query-svc into a separate service. Root cause for high p50+p99 is heavy projection + RBAC evaluation hot paths in query-svc. Splitting should isolate slow libs and reduce tail. Thoughts?

Maya Patel: +1 on isolation. Concern: double hop for small panels will add latency. Need numbers on how much overhead the extra RPC adds.

Jon Rivera: Can we do a thin-proxy pattern? Renderer handles layout + local caching, calls query-svc for aggregates only. RBAC: move coarse-grained auth to edge, keep fine-grained checks that need DB lookups in query-svc.

Sam O'Neill: For RBAC we should avoid duplicating expensive checks. Idea: cache decision tokens per session (short TTL) in renderer. TTL 30s? 1m? :thinking:

Alex Kim: Agreed on token cache. Example config sketch:
```
renderer.auth_cache_ttl: 30s
renderer.fallback_on_query_error: true
querysvc.return_partial: true
```

Maya Patel: What about multi-tenant KV cache? If renderer keeps prefix KV cache for panel templates it helps. But eviction/consistency across rollouts is tricky.

Jon Rivera: Tradeoffs: duplication of KV cache increases memory but reduces load on query-svc. For sensitive endpoints we must ensure cache keys include tenant and permission hash.

Sam O'Neill: Security check: include permission-hash in cache key, example: `cache_key = fmt("%s:%s:%s", tenant_id, perm_hash, panel_id)`

Alex Kim: Ops concerns — need rollout plan with canary and circuit-breaker. Proposal: start with 10% -> 30% -> 100% across non-critical namespaces, monitor p50/p99 & error rate.

Maya Patel: Add telemetry: per-route latency, cache hit ratio, RBAC-miss-rate, and auth-cache-staleness metric.

Jon Rivera: Also need fallback policy: if renderer can't reach query-svc, render degraded UI with cached data and a banner. UX to decide wording.

Sam O'Neill: I'll draft a cutover checklist: feature flag, telemetry, canary, kill-switch, migration of auth-cache, DB migrations (none), infra changes (new service + autoscale policy).

Alex Kim: Thanks — @Sam can you post checklist as PR? I'll loop in @infra to provision namespaces. :thumbsup: 

ops-bot: deploy-notice: canary started for renderer v0.1 -> 100 requests routed to renderer-canary

Maya Patel: saw canary traffic :eyes: initial p50 +8ms, backend tail p99 improved ~22ms, one 502 from renderer due to protobuf parsing (fix incoming)

Alex Kim: update: remove protobuf lib in renderer, use JSON wire for now. Keep rolling.

Sam O'Neill: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/1234 — contains checklist + basic telemetry scaffolding

Jon Rivera: Next steps: perf test harness that drives 5k concurrent dashboards, simulate auth cache TTLs, and measure cost delta (CPU/mem) across renderer replicas.

Maya Patel: Sounds good. I'll own perf harness. Tagging owners for RBAC: @Jon and @Sam. End of thread.
